# 0.0.0-dev.1: ???? (??-??-????)

## Breaking changes

- support-this now requires Quarto 1.10 or later.

## Features

- `support-this` provides support buttons for various funding platforms directly into your documents. 
  - You can configure multiple platforms and custom links through the document's YAML front matter or a `FUNDING.yml` file.
- `heading: false` leaves out the support section's heading.

## Bug fixes

- `debug` now defaults to `false`, so renders no longer print `[support-this]`
  messages unless you set `debug: true`.
- `display: badge` now shows badges for platform names and accounts that
  contain `-` or `_`, such as Ko-fi or `coatless-quarto`. Previously, shields.io
  showed "404: badge not found" for them, and an underscore came out as a
  space.
- support-this now shows a distinct icon for every platform in HTML: the
  logos of GitHub Sponsors, Patreon, Ko-fi, Buy Me a Coffee, Liberapay, Open
  Collective and LFX Mentorship, and generic icons for Tidelift, IssueHunt,
  Polar, thanks.dev and custom links. Previously, several platforms shared the
  same placeholder icon.
- support-this now follows the page's light or dark theme in HTML. Previously,
  the section was always a light box, even on dark pages.
- support-this now puts a space between the platform name and the account in
  HTML links ("Patreon: coatless" instead of "Patreon:coatless").
- support-this now renders the support section in Typst, PDF, Word and other
  non-HTML formats as a note callout titled with `heading`. Previously, it was
  a plain heading followed by a list.
- support-this now leaves the platform icons out of PDF output, where LaTeX's
  default fonts showed them as missing characters. With
  `display: icon-username`, the platform name takes the icon's place.
- `use_funding_yml: true` no longer adds an empty support section when
  `FUNDING.yml` has no accounts, as in GitHub's default template.
- `platforms` now takes precedence over `FUNDING.yml` for a platform set in
  both. Previously, the `FUNDING.yml` accounts replaced the document's.
- `use_funding_yml: true` now also finds `FUNDING.yml` or `.github/FUNDING.yml`
  at the project root and at the root of the git repository. Previously, only
  the document's folder was searched, so pages in subfolders and projects in
  `docs/` found nothing.
- `use_funding_yml: true` now reads `FUNDING.yml` values the same way as the
  document's `platforms`, so a numeric account such as `ko_fi: 12345` is no
  longer skipped.
- `custom` links without a scheme, such as `example.com/donate`, now go to
  `https://example.com/donate`. Previously, they were relative links that led
  nowhere.
- `platforms` values that contain spaces now stay one account. Previously,
  `custom: "https://example.com/donate here"` became three links.
- A `::: {.support-this}` div now always marks where the section goes,
  whatever `position` says, and the section appears only there. Previously,
  the div was only used with `position: custom`; with `top` or `bottom` the
  section appeared twice, and with the default the div was ignored.
- `position: custom` now warns when the document has no `::: {.support-this}`
  div, instead of silently leaving the section out.
- In RevealJS, a section placed with a `::: {.support-this}` div now stays on
  the div's slide. Previously, it split that slide in two.
- `position` and `display` now warn about an unknown value, such as `Top` or
  `icons`, and use their defaults. Previously, an unknown `position` left the
  section out without a message.
- `platforms` now warns about unknown keys, such as `kofi` instead of `ko_fi`.
  Previously, they were silently skipped.
- `use_funding_yml: true` now warns when it finds no `FUNDING.yml`.
- Accounts and URLs under `platforms` now keep `--`, `---`, `...` and quotes
  as typed. Previously, Markdown's smart punctuation turned
  `https://example.com/a--b` into a link with an en dash.
- `heading`, `description` and accounts that contain `<`, `&` or `"` now show
  as typed in HTML. Previously, they could break the section's markup.
- support-this now lists links by platform name, with custom links last.
  Previously, they were sorted by internal key, so custom links came first.
- support-this now works alongside other extensions that have a Lua module
  named `platforms`. Previously, it could pick up the other extension's module
  and silently leave out the support section.

## Documentation

- The README and home page now document the `display`, `position` and `debug`
  options and where `FUNDING.yml` is looked for, and give the default `heading`
  as "Support This Project".
- The README and demo page now use `description`, the option the extension
  reads, instead of `message`. The README and home page no longer list a
  `truncated` option, which never existed.
- The README's multiple-accounts example is now valid YAML.
- The docs sidebar no longer links to a FAQ page that doesn't exist.
- The docs site has new pages for each display mode, top and custom
  placement, and all 12 platforms. The home page has a platform reference
  table and troubleshooting tips, and the multiformat page is also rendered to
  Typst and Word.
- The `FUNDING.yml` page now explains where the file is looked for and how it
  combines with `platforms`.
- The docs examples use real accounts instead of placeholder handles.
